Hannah / team — quick answers below; attaching the test artifacts and summaries.

1) RTO / RPO
- Dedicated deployment (reserved capacity, customer VPC option): targeted RTO for region-level failure is 15 minutes for control-plane failover and traffic re-routing; application-level recovery (warm caches) typically < 5 minutes for new sessions. RPO is effectively 0 for user requests (stateless requests are re-issued; for customer-managed persistent stores we rely on the customer's DB replication). For stateful in-memory KV caching, we use prefix/KV caching with replication and asynchronous checkpoints — expect near-zero loss for short-lived sessions; worst-case temporary session loss for uncommitted in-flight generation.
- Hosted (multi-tenant): targeted RTO for platform incidents is 60 minutes (failover + capacity resharding), RPO dependent on caching layer: recommended to use our persistent storage connector for any critical persisted artifacts.

2) Disaster recovery exercises
- Cadence: annual full DR test + quarterly tabletop exercises.
- Most recent full DR: 2024-11-06 (scope: region-level failover simulation, API ingress reroute to secondary region, verification of service mesh and KV warmup). Outcome: routing and control-plane automation met RTO target for Dedicated (15m). DR test summary attached: DR_Test_Summary_2024.pdf.

3) Independent assurance
- SOC 2 Type II report (period: 2024-03 to 2025-03) available under NDA — summary attached (SOC2_Report_2024.pdf).
- Penetration test high-level findings: third-party pen-test (external vendor) completed 2024-09; no critical findings, several medium findings remediated within 30 days. We can share the executive summary (PenTest_Summary_2024.pdf).

4) Key management & encryption
- At rest: AES-256 for model weights, embeddings, and cache snapshots.
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ (preferred TLS 1.3) for all network traffic.
- Customer-managed keys: supported for Dedicated and Private deployments via integrations with AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and enterprise HSMs (PKCS#11). CMK mode allows customers to rotate/disable keys per their policy; Redwood has an option to use envelope encryption with customer KEK.

5) Audit logs
- Retention: default platform retention 90 days; export capability to customer-owned S3/Blob for long-term retention (we commonly advise 7+ years for financial audits).
- Tamper-evidence: logs are signed and stored with checksum-based immutability flags; exports to customer storage are object-locked where supported.
- Access: full audit trail includes request metadata, model and route used, latency, and operator actions; can stream to SIEMs via Kafka or native cloud log sinks.

6) Third-party dependencies
- Primary infra: AWS us-east-1 and us-west-2 (multi-region by default for Dedicated). We rely on AWS managed network and storage (S3, EBS). Where customers require different providers, Redwood Private supports on-prem and alternative cloud regions. We maintain contractual SLAs with our cloud partners for infrastructure availability; Redwood's customer-facing SLA covers the Redwood service layer.

Attachments included: SOC2_Report_2024.pdf, DR_Test_Summary_2024.pdf, PenTest_Summary_2024.pdf.
